title: Pink Halloween Party Decor
intro: Halloween does not have to be black and orange to count. Hot pink pumpkins, ghost print tablecloths and tall pink candles make a table people photograph before they eat. Spooky is optional. Cute is the point.

sections.heading: Start with the tablecloth
paragraphs: The pink ghost Halloween tablecloths come in a 3 pack, and that matters more than it sounds. One goes on the food table, one on the drinks table and one gets folded away for the next party, or for the moment somebody knocks over the punch. The print is little white ghosts carrying candy buckets, plus bats and stars.

Check the dimensions on the listing against your table before you open anything. Plastic tablecloths are usually cut for a standard rectangle, so a round table will hang uneven. Tape the corners underneath with a bit of painter's tape. It keeps kids from dragging the whole spread down when they lunge for a cupcake.

sections.heading: Pumpkins and candles down the middle
paragraphs: The hot pink artificial pumpkins come as a set of seven in a few sizes, which makes them easy to group. Odd numbers look natural. They are fake, so they last for years and nobody deals with a soft pumpkin on November third.

The hot pink taper candles come four to a pack. Stand them in holders you already own, glass, brass, white, whatever is in the cabinet, and line them up next to the pumpkins. Pink tapers beside pink pumpkins look like you planned it for weeks. You did not. Nobody needs to know.

Now the safety part, because the tablecloth is plastic and balloons pop. Keep lit candles well back from the edge of the cloth and far from the balloon garland, and away from anywhere a costume sleeve or set of wings might swing past. Never leave them burning in an empty room. With kids running around, leave the tapers unlit or use battery tea lights.

sections.heading: Balloons and windows
paragraphs: The pink and purple Halloween balloon garland kit gives you the biggest impact for the least effort. You blow up the balloons, thread them onto the strip and bunch them as you go. Hang it over a doorway or swag it along the front edge of the food table.

Give yourself an hour for the balloons, or recruit someone with better lungs. A hand pump saves your dignity and your dizzy head. Use removable hooks so the wall paint survives the party, and keep the finished garland out of direct sun so the balloons do not go soft before guests arrive.

The pink Halloween window clings are the easiest piece of all. Ghosts, pumpkins, candy and a little rainbow on one sheet, and they stick to glass with no glue. Put them on the front window so trick or treaters see them, or on a mirror by the snack table. Clean the glass first or they slide.

sections.heading: Pulling it together without spending a lot
paragraphs: You do not need every piece. The tablecloth and pumpkins alone turn a plain table into a pink Halloween table. Add your own white plates, a cake stand you already own and a bowl of candy, and it looks finished.

The first time I set this up, I put the balloon garland way too close to the candles and spent the whole party side eyeing it instead of eating. Move the balloons first, then light anything. Afterward, wipe the tablecloth down if it survived, peel the clings back onto their sheet and box up the pumpkins for next year.
Everything in the styled and lifestyle photos that is not on the list, the pumpkins, mugs, lights and furniture, is styling extras, so use what you already own.
